Build a collaborative document editor that allows multiple users to edit documents in real-time. 

The system should support rich text formatting including bold, italic, headings, bullet lists, and code blocks. Users should be able to see each other's cursors and selections in real-time with different colors assigned to each collaborator.

Documents should auto-save every 30 seconds and also save when the user stops typing for more than 2 seconds. There should be a version history feature that lets users browse and restore previous versions.

Access control is important — document owners should be able to invite collaborators with different permission levels: viewer (read-only), commenter (can add comments but not edit), and editor (full editing access). Sharing should work via email invitations or shareable links with configurable expiration.

The editor needs to work offline. When a user goes offline, they should still be able to edit, and their changes should sync automatically when connectivity is restored, with conflict resolution handled gracefully.

For the backend, we need a WebSocket server for real-time collaboration, a REST API for document CRUD operations, and a PostgreSQL database for persistence. The system should handle at least 100 concurrent editors per document without degradation.

Error handling should be robust — if the WebSocket connection drops, the client should attempt reconnection with exponential backoff. If a save fails, the user should see a clear error message with a retry option.

The frontend should be built with React and use a CRDT-based data structure for conflict-free collaborative editing. The UI should be responsive and work well on both desktop and mobile devices.
